req.title: Register requires password
req.statement: The system shall render the register form with an error message when POST /auth/register omits the password.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-005 requires that POST /auth/register with a missing password field renders the register form with the exact error message 'Password is required.' and returns an HTTP 2xx status. Three tests are designed: (1) a positive case confirming the error message appears when username is provided but password is omitted; (2) a negative case confirming that providing both username and password does NOT produce the error message (contrast path); (3) a boundary case confirming that an empty-string password (distinct from a missing key) also triggers the same error. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant-mutation, string-mutation, and boolean-negation mutants.

tests.name: test_register_missing_password_shows_error
preconditions: Flask app is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
actions: POST /auth/register with username='newuser99' and no password field
expected: Response body contains exactly 'Password is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-005: system shall render register form with error when password is omitted
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_missing_password_shows_error():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'newuser99'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Password is required.' in r.data
    assert b'Username is required.' not in r.data

test_register_missing_password_shows_error()

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_with_valid_credentials_no_password_error():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'brandnewuser', 'password': 'securepass'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    assert b'Password is required.' not in r.data

test_register_with_valid_credentials_no_password_error()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_missing_password_exact_error_text():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'testuser42'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Password is required.' in r.data
    assert b'Username is required.' not in r.data
    assert b'already registered' not in r.data
    assert b'302' not in r.data

tests.name: test_register_missing_both_fields_shows_username_error_not_password
preconditions: Flask app is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
actions: POST /auth/register with neither username nor password
Verify that username error fires first (short-circuit) and password error does NOT appear
expected: b'Password is required.' absent (username check short-circuits)
trace: R-FLASKR-005: boundary — validates that password error is only shown when username IS provided; guards against mutation swapping the if/elif order
